## Final Project Definition

The project you are designing here is **your** final project — either one of the ideas on the **[Final Project Specifications](../projects/final_project.qmd)** page, or a project idea the instructor has approved. Read that page end to end (overview, required showcase sections, rubric, and the idea you picked) before you start this exercise.

## Assignment Overview

Anyone can build an agentic system with Claude Code or Open Code.  _Can you build one that is reliable, safe, cost effective and meets all the requirements every time it's run?_  It's time to put on your AI architect hat and address LLM/RAG shortcomings with a good agentic AI design.

## Rubric

This is a 500 point exercise.  It's an assessment of how much you have learned up to this point.  Please take it seriously.  It's as important as the project output.  You should complete this Quarto markdown file (.qmd) and turn it in along (as .qmd) with a quarto rendered PDF version (.pdf).  Add `format: pdf` to the yaml header of this file and then run `quarto render yourfilename.qmd` to build the PDF.

## Important Note

This work must be done 100% without assistance from any AI.  I need to know that *YOU* have learned the material. I know that Claude knows it.  **Any use of AI will be easily detected and will be treated as an Honor Code violation.  Please take this seriously.**

## Introduction

Unlike the mid-term, there is no single specification for everyone — so before you list requirements, tell me what you are building.  Name the project you chose: one of the ideas on the [Final Project Specifications](../projects/final_project.qmd) page, **or** a project the instructor has approved (say so, and when it was approved).

Then write a few paragraphs (in prose) explaining what you are trying to accomplish.  Who is the user?  What problem do they have today, and what will they be able to do with your solution that they cannot do now?  What is in scope and — just as important — what is out of scope?  What does a successful run look like?  Finally, make the case for why this problem **needs a multi-agent design** rather than a single prompt or a script.

The project we have chosen is 35.4.12 Sports: Opponent Tendencies Analyst from the list of ideas on the Final Project Specifications page.

The goal of this project is to giving a coaching staff or game-prep analyst a single, evidence-backed opponent tendencies report for an upcoming **SPORTS ORG OF OUR CHOSING** game since more often than not, play-by-play data and qualitative context in beat-reporter coverage and coach quotes never merge.
